_doc: The hatched 'Waiting for you' slice of the donut: time the main session waited on a person (timeline categories human_wait:*). 'parts' names each kind; a part with in_ring false (a parked session) is counted apart, like idle time, and not drawn. 'rules' are deterministic tips to wait on the person less; a rule fires for its part when min_count episodes (and min_questions turns that ended with a question, min_p50_s median) are there. 'for' says who acts: 'you' (the person: settings, CLAUDE.md, notifications, how tasks are handed over) or 'agent' (how the agent should behave); the page lists them apart, up to 3 each. Placeholders: {n} episodes, {total} time, {p50} median, {longest}, {q} stops that ended with a question, {q_total} their time, {top} the most frequent command or tool, {top_n} its count, {sessions}. saving = saving_fraction x saving_basis, where saving_basis is 'seconds' (the part's time, default), 'questions_s' (the time after stops that ended with a question) or 'extra_p50' ((episodes - sessions) x median: one wait per session instead of one per episode). Omit saving_fraction when there is no honest estimate; the saving is the person's waiting time, not agent time.

parts.label: Your next message
parts.help: The agent finished its turn and waited until you wrote again.

parts.label: Permission prompts
parts.help: A quick tool sat far longer than it runs, in a session that asks for permission: inferred as a permission prompt.

parts.label: Approval gate
parts.help: Commands run through a human-approval gate (GATE_REASON=...) waited for the approval.

parts.label: Questions to you
parts.help: AskUserQuestion, plan approval or a request for a human.

parts.label: Session parked
parts.help: The session was parked or you were marked away.

rules.title: Add allow-rules for commands that keep asking
rules.why: {n} tool calls stood still on a permission prompt ({total}, median {p50}). Each one stops the run until you click.
rules.after: permissions.allow in .claude/settings.json lists the safe commands (the fewer-permission-prompts skill drafts the list)
rules.assumption: allow-rules remove most prompts; the rest are commands you want to see

rules.title: Tell agents which decisions they may take alone
rules.why: {q} of {n} stops ended with a question to you; the run waited {q_total} for those answers.
rules.evidence: {q} turns whose last text ends with '?', followed by your next message.
rules.before: 'Shall I also deploy?' and the run stops until you answer
rules.after: a short 'decide yourself' list in CLAUDE.md (deploy or not, naming, how far to go); the agent takes the default, says so, and keeps going
rules.assumption: upper bound: with a default the run goes on instead of waiting for the answer
rules.source: Claude Code docs, Memory (CLAUDE.md is read at the start of every session): https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory

rules.title: Get a push on your phone when an agent stops
rules.why: The agent finished its turn {n} times and waited a median {p50} until you wrote again (longest {longest}).
rules.before: you see that the agent is done only when you next look at its terminal
rules.after: a Stop hook (turn finished) and a Notification hook (needs your input) send a push; you answer within minutes
rules.source: Claude Code docs, Hooks (Stop and Notification events): https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks

rules.title: Give follow-up tasks and done-criteria up front
rules.why: The agent stopped {n} times and waited a median {p50} for your next message (longest {longest}).
rules.before: one task per message; the agent idles until you look again
rules.after: the brief lists the next steps and when the work is done; a queue the agent can pull from

rules.title: Batch gated commands into one approval
rules.why: {n} gated commands each waited for an approval ({total}, median {p50}); every one interrupts you.
rules.after: related read-only checks in one gated command; one approval per task, not per command
rules.assumption: one approval per session instead of one per command; each extra approval cost the median wait

rules.title: Ask all open questions in one batch
rules.why: The agent stopped {n} times to ask you something ({total}, median {p50}).
rules.evidence: {n} questions or plan approvals in {sessions}; most often {top} ({top_n}x).
rules.before: one question, wait, another question, wait
rules.after: the agent collects its questions and asks them together, with a recommended default for each
rules.assumption: one round of questions per session; each extra round cost the median wait
